newsitem.title: USA: Hartford to get AHL team, the Binghamton Rangers.
newsitem.headline: Hartford to get AHL team, the Binghamton Rangers.

text.p: The Binghamton Rangers of the American Hockey League will move to Hartford and play next season at the Civic Center, state officials said Wednesday.

The relocated team, which does not yet have a name and is essentially a farm team for the National Hockey League's New York Rangers, was recently purchased by Madison Square Garden Limited Partners (MSG).
MSG also owns the New York Rangers, the National Basketball Association's New York Knicks, and a TV cable network.

The new team should bring Hartford $4.0 million to $7.0 million a year in economic benefits, said an official of Connecticut Development Authority which leases the Civic Center coliseum from Hartford.
Connecticut last month lost its only major league sports franchise when the NHL's Hartford Whalers moved to North Carolina.
The 61-year-old AHL is considered the main source of player development for the NHL.
Under the agreement, MSG will provide Connecticut with at least $500,000 worth of cable advertising to promote economic development in the state, a CDA official said.
MSG's New York Rangers and New York Knicks will also each play one exhibition game at the Civic Center.
MSG will also produce an unspecified number of additional sports, entertainment and other events in the Civic Center.
The MSG proposal is for 10 years, with a six-year renewal option.
The deal is expected to close in the next 60 days, and it calls for MSG to operate concessions, sales and marketing for the Civic Center.

"Bringing in these different events, it means more jobs and a better impact on downtown and the surrounding areas," Hartford Mayor Mike Peters was quoted as saying in the Hartford Courant on Wednesday. "It was a hard deal to pass up."
